title: Put a long serving board away at the back of a board rack, behind two boards leaning on its rail
keywords: slide in from the open end
instruction: Put the long board away at the back of the rack, without taking the other boards out.
context: In most kitchens, boards stand on edge in a rack and lean back on its rail. Putting one away at the back, where the longest board goes, is a one-handed hold and a one-handed insert: tip the leaning boards toward you with one hand and keep them there, slip the new board in behind them with the other, then let them lean back onto it. Let go too early and the gap closes; tip them past upright and they fall out of the rack.
setup: Two YAM arms with parallel grippers, bases 61 cm apart at the near edge of a table. Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x straight out, y to the left. Board rack (beech, 2.0 kg): floor 13 x 51 cm (x by y), 1.2 cm thick, near edge at x 28; a 1 x 1 cm lip along that edge; a 2 x 2 cm back rail with its top 10 cm above the table on two 2 x 2 cm end posts, 10 cm of floor between lip and rail and 47 cm between the posts (y -33 to +14). Two bamboo serving boards (24 x 16 x 1.0 cm, 0.27 kg each) stand on their long edges in the rack between y -12 and +12, the front one's foot against the lip, leaning back on the rail at about 41 degrees. Long bamboo board (32 x 12 x 1.2 cm, 0.30 kg): standing on its long edge in a beech drying stand at (20, -4): base 34 x 6 x 1 cm with two 34 x 2 x 3 cm jaws leaving a 1.5 cm slot. Each trial shifts the rack and the boards in it by one row of a 7-row table (up to 1 cm in x and 5 cm in y; README).
scoring: Checked with a ruler and a protractor once nothing has moved for 1 s and both grippers are at least 3 cm from every board. 1.0: all three boards stand on the rack floor (lowest point within 3 mm of it) and lie between lip, rail and end posts, the long board's foot nearest the rail and the two short boards leaning back on it, 5 to 40 degrees (the long board may lean -5 to 40). 0.5: the long board is in the rack but the stack is not back on it: the same checks, but the short boards stand upright (-5 to 5 degrees) instead of leaning back, or the long board is in front of or between them. 0 otherwise, including a board still held, a board on the table or flat, or either short board's lowest point ever more than 1 cm above or below the rack floor during the trial (taken out; putting it back does not undo that).
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Stand the long board back in the drying stand, the two short boards in the rack against the lip, leaning on the rail.
fidelity: Real-size boards, rack and stand; masses from bamboo's density. Each board is one rigid box with square edges, the rack and stand are box assemblies, friction 1.2 everywhere. Two boards in the rack, not a full set, to keep the trial short.
